RESOLVED 2026-08-10 (was the top open question): 'whether C2's quality losses are mid-layer-read failures or retrieval-recall failures'. ANSWER: benchmark-dependent. BABILong qa1/qa2 -> retrieval dominates (recall@12 only 22.9-63.2%). RULER -> retrieval is ~0 (recall 99-100%) and the whole loss is the read (deployed -3 to -12pp). If A02 continues, two candidates, NEITHER CoMem-specific: (a) sublinear retrieval -- selection is the dominant per-query cost at 1M (1014.8 ms vs 678 ms read); (b) a better selector than top-12 iter_bm25 -- it misses the gold support on 37-77% of BABILong qa1/qa2 samples. Both would benefit plain text-RAG identically, so neither supports a CoMem thesis.

depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.question: Phase-1's C1-vs-C2 moved FOUR variables at once (verified from on-disk cell configs: C1 no_retrieval=True/selector=None/topk=None/resume_j=0/lora=None vs C2 no_retrieval=False/selector=iter_bm25/topk=12/resume_j=12/lora=flagship). Were C2's quality losses MID-LAYER-READ failures (A02's thesis) or RETRIEVAL-RECALL failures (a property of top-12 iter_bm25, unrelated to CoMem)?
depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.verdict: BOTH ARE REAL AND WHICH DOMINATES IS DECIDED BY THE BENCHMARK. BABILong qa1/qa2 -> RETRIEVAL dominates (54.9-78.6%). RULER -> READ dominates (retrieval ~0, recall 99-100%). BABILong qa5 -> neither step significant.
depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.headline: Phase-1's four 'decisive C1 wins' on BABILong qa1/qa2 (-35 to -55pp) are MOSTLY a retrieval/pack-narrowing artifact, NOT evidence about mid-layer reading. A02's read thesis was only ever properly tested by RULER, where the DEPLOYED read costs a significant but modest -3 to -12pp with retrieval held identical.

arms.c1_pack_all: phase-1 C1 (on disk): j=0, no LoRA, packs ALL chunks, no selector
arms.j0_top12: NEW: j=0, no LoRA, top-12 iter_bm25 == matched-pack text-RAG
arms.j12_frozen: NEW: j=12, NO LoRA, SAME top-12 pack -- this is what breaks the depth<->LoRA confound the cost gate called irreducible
arms.c2_comem: phase-1 C2 (on disk): j=12 + flagship Read-LoRA, same top-12 pack

depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.steps: retrieval=c1->j0_top12; read_depth=j0_top12->j12_frozen; read_lora=j12_frozen->c2_comem; read_deployed=j0_top12->c2_comem (the like-for-like shipped read). retrieval+read_deployed EXACTLY partitions the total c1->c2 change and read_depth+read_lora EXACTLY equals read_deployed (both asserted to 1e-6 on all 10 cells), so nothing is double-counted.

retrieval_recall_at_12.method: HIT iff EVERY gold-support chunk is in the top-12 iter_bm25 pack; decided INDEPENDENTLY of answer accuracy; flagship selector + harness gold locator both imported unmodified
retrieval_recall_at_12.ruler: niah_mk1x16k 100.0% [96.2,100.0] | niah_mk1x32k 99.0% [94.6,99.8] | variable_tracking NOT MEASURABLE (0 gold-locatable)
retrieval_recall_at_12.interpretation: the retrieval channel is wide open on BABILong (misses gold on 37-77% of samples, degrading with length) and closed on RULER -- exactly matching where each cause dominates

depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.NEW_FINDING_adapter_dependence: Mid-depth resume is almost ENTIRELY adapter-supplied: j12_frozen scores 0.0-3.0% on RULER while c2_comem scores 88-96% (read_depth -97 to -100pp, read_lora +87 to +95pp). Resuming at layer 12 on chunk-local hiddens is non-functional untrained. This is clean, previously unmeasured, and is a fact about distillation, not about memory efficiency. NOTE it is task-dependent: read_lora is n.s. on BABILong qa2 (+4.0, -1.0).
depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.conditional_on_recall: Confirms retrieval is causal (penalty always larger on MISS than HIT: qa1x16k -45.7 vs -36.7; qa2x16k -43.8 vs -21.3; j0_top12 collapses to 5-20% on MISS) AND qualifies it (the retrieval step stays significantly negative on the HIT subset too, so 'gold chunk in pack' is NOT sufficient -- narrowing 30-60 chunks to 12 also removes distractor/aggregation context). On RULER the retrieval step is +2.02 ns on the 99-sample HIT subset.
depth_vs_retrieval_quality_gate.confound_KEPT_stated_plainly: There is NO arm here that isolates depth with a matched-quality adapter. j12_frozen runs j=12 WITHOUT the adapter distilled for it, so it is a LOWER BOUND on depth-12 capability, not a fair depth arm; read_deployed bundles depth+adapter. Both are reported. The read_depth -97pp on RULER must NOT be read as 'depth costs 97pp' -- it means 'untrained depth-12 resume is non-functional'. The defensible depth-effect numbers are the read_deployed ones (-3 to -12pp). Removing this confound needs a j=0 control LoRA = TRAINING, out of scope for an eval gate.
